chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdurrahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Hearts are created with a love for the one who benefits them and a hatred for the one who harms them.
ai.seo_question: What is the natural disposition of the human heart according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the human heart is naturally inclined to love those who confer benefit and to dislike those who cause harm, a principle rooted in the concept of *fitrah* (innate disposition). This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the psychological and spiritual mechanism of attachment, suggesting that human relationships are fundamentally guided by this intrinsic sense of utility and well-being. It serves as a foundational insight for understanding social dynamics and spiritual affinity in Shia thought.

en.hubeali: H 14588 – From him, from Ahmad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from some of our companions, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘
It is inherent in the hearts to love the one who benefits it, and hate the one who harms it’.
en.sarwar: 140. From him, from Ahmad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from some of our companions, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said:
‘It is inherent in the hearts to love the one who benefits it, and hate the one who harms it’.
